D06-B — Partial applicability decision User's product decision: allow partial-applicability property editing. Behavior to materialize: - Show eligible/total and explicit skipped-root reasons before commit. - Uniform/Mixed are computed over eligible targets; Partial applicability is a separate axis. - Only semantically inapplicable targets may be excluded. - If a target that is semantically applicable is locked, permission-denied, stale, or invalid, reject the entire eligible cohort before mutation. - Commit all eligible targets atomically or none. - Return truthful per-target results. - Do not add a FieldId, PropertyValue, or Operation for this policy. Authority condition: FC-00X-C currently records D06-B / eligible-only editing as OPEN; FC-01A warns that showing a subset does not itself authorize executing it. This audit records the user's explicit decision, but does not pretend current Authority has already been updated. Before product implementation, route a narrow D06-B authority update through its owner. ## 2. D07 — Multi-operation intent and one Undo Source/architecture findings: - 07-02 describes a local provisional UndoIntent and finalizing a user-visible HistoryGroup only after required forward Operations succeed; zero-apply failure discards the provisional intent, fully compensated failure does not create a successful user Undo item. - 07-14 says IntentPlan / IntentCommitSegment / UndoIntent / ApplyBatchResult are orchestration/local history concepts, not a canonical global Transaction. Each Operation retains its own generation, commit stamp, ChangeSet and publication. Cross-client/crash whole-intent atomic visibility is not claimed. - FC-00X-C explicitly leaves D07 cross-Operation atomicity/one-Undo OPEN. - operation\_payload.hpp has multi-target SetTransformsOp.items\[\] and PatchPropertiesOp.patches\[\]; this supports representing some homogeneous multi-target intents in one Operation, but does not prove heterogeneous multi-Operation intent is atomic. - EditorHistory has PreparedEntry, forward/inverse operations, before/after expectations, and a submit port accepting spans of Operations. This is promising structure, but these types alone do not prove a passing end-to-end guarantee. - Existing editor\_history\_test.cpp contains unit tests for undo/redo compensation and rejection behavior, but this review did not run them and did not establish that a user intent spanning several distinct operations yields one History unit under every failure point. Decision: the product requirement remains one coherent local all-or-nothing user intent and one user-visible Undo unit. Reuse the existing coordinator/HistoryGroup path if actual source tests prove it. Do not introduce a generic canonical Transaction. If current implementation cannot meet the contract, prepare a narrow D07/History amendment before implementing commands that need multiple distinct Operations. Until then, single-Operation multi-target commands may proceed where their existing accepted operation supports the whole cohort; multi-Operation commands without proven support stay unavailable. ## 3. FC-02 TextEdit / Escape decision User accepted: - Double-click/Edit Text targets the actual hit text object, not a previously selected arbitrary primary. - TextEdit replaces the multi-root edit cohort with one owning root plus focused text target. - On TextEdit commit/cancel, leave the owning object selected; do not silently restore the previous multi-selection. - Escape cancels the active TextEdit/IME composition first and must not also clear selection or leave container scope in the same key event. Existing Text/IME contract says composition/caret/focus are transient; cancelling an uncommitted IME composition is a canonical no-op; committed text flows through TextEditSession → RichTextDelta → EditRichText; interruption must not auto-commit transient text. Source inspection confirms TextEditSession is owned by InteractionRuntime, shares the existing session manager and typed command/history lane, and has an owner API finish(keepEditor=false). It does not alone prove which caller maps double-click/Escape to these semantics. Bind the accepted behavior at the existing input/target/session owner and add regression tests; do not implement this in UI-only code. ## 4. Initial property-by-kind source matrix Important distinction: the frozen Field Registry and operation\_state\_validator.cpp establish declared applicability/type validation, not by themselves the complete read-provider, capability resolver, command wiring, and History proof. This matrix is a starting inventory, not an assertion of end-to-end support. | Property | Field ID / value | Declared applicable kinds | Validator evidence | First-phase disposition | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Visible | 0x00000001 / Bool | Shape, Image, VectorPath, RichText, VectorStroke, DabStroke, Connector, Sticky, Group | supportsField currently returns true for all kinds except Section via the special Section branch | Read/write provider and command path must be traced; do not assume UI toggle is ready | | Locked | 0x00000002 / Bool | Shape, Image, VectorPath, RichText, VectorStroke, DabStroke, Connector, Sticky, Group | same broad validator rule; Section special branch excludes locked | High-risk capability because lock affects subsequent command eligibility; defer until owner behavior confirmed | | Opacity | 0x00000003 / F32\_0\_1 | Shape, Image, VectorPath, RichText, Connector, Sticky, Section | validator accepts Float and declares Section only field 0x3/0x100 | Candidate for initial multi-edit if actual read/command/History chain is complete | | BlendMode | 0x00000004 / BlendModeValue | Shape, Image, VectorPath, RichText, Connector, Sticky | validator accepts BlendModeValue; not applicable to Section, Group, strokes | Candidate only after actual read and command path traced | | FillStyle | 0x00000100 / FillStyleValue | Shape, VectorPath, Sticky, Section | validator accepts FillStyleValue for these kinds; Section has special allowance | Candidate for eligible-subset policy if read/write owner is complete | | StrokeStyle | 0x00000101 / StrokeStyleValue | Shape, VectorPath, Connector, Sticky | validator accepts StrokeStyleValue for these kinds; Section does not allow this field | Candidate; Connector must use its accepted typed style semantics | | Connector start/end decoration | 0x00000200 / 0x00000201 ConnectorDecorationValue | Connector only | validator accepts ConnectorDecorationValue for Connector | Connector-only; never infer cross-kind applicability | Field registry source: [field\_registry\_v1.yaml](https://github.com/Mostorm-Labs/axiom/blob/2fee75f66a7f96f6aac834228ede372a9abda59a/schema/axiom/v1/registry/field_registry_v1.yaml).
Validator source: [operation\_state\_validator.cpp](https://github.com/Mostorm-Labs/axiom/blob/2fee75f66a7f96f6aac834228ede372a9abda59a/runtime/semantic/src/operation_state_validator.cpp). The first implementation package must extend this matrix with exact property read owner, capability provider, mutation command/Operation, History path, and test paths from the actual checkout. Missing provider/API is Indeterminate/Unavailable, not Unsupported, unless accepted semantics explicitly declare the property inapplicable. ## 5. MSE test binding Keep MSE-01..MSE-27 from the parent behavior contract and decision addendum. Bind them to real owner paths: - MSE-01..06: normalized selection roots, multi-target transform, property read and uniform/mixed aggregation. - MSE-07, 19, 21: explicit eligible subset, eligible/total, Mixed and Partial orthogonality. - MSE-08, 17: kind-specific field/Connector semantics. - MSE-09, 20: applicable target locked/stale/permission-denied rejects the eligible cohort with zero mutation. - MSE-10, 23: invalid target and failure at each operation/history reservation boundary leave Document, Scene publication, History cursor and redo branch unchanged. - MSE-11: cancellation produces no canonical write or History unit. - MSE-12, 13, 22: Undo after selection changes, Redo, and multi-operation single-Undo behavior. - MSE-14, 27: stale selection/semantic generation rejects or re-resolves before commit. - MSE-15: multiple distinct Operations without accepted atomic path remain unavailable. - MSE-16: selection/Inspector refresh is read-only. - MSE-18: single-object transform, Section, Image Crop and Connector regression. - MSE-24, 25: actual-hit TextEdit target and Escape/IME precedence. - MSE-26: missing property provider cannot enable UI. Tests must assert real document snapshots, scene/semantic generations, History cursor/redo availability, and per-target results; UI-only tests are not sufficient. ## 6. Closure outcome - D06-B: user decision recorded; formal current-Authority acceptance still required. - D07: architectural path identified, source-level end-to-end proof not established; inspect/execute actual tests before deciding whether a narrow amendment is needed. - FC-02 TextEdit behavior: product behavior accepted; target/input/Escape wiring and tests remain to be bound. - Property matrix: validator and frozen registry audited at main HEAD; end-to-end read/capability/command/History matrix still needs implementation-branch completion. - MSE-01..MSE-27: behavior cases are defined and mapped at the family level; exact source test paths and test runs remain required. No source code was changed and no tests/builds were executed by this review. No Phase 2 implementation authorization or product Gate PASS is issued.
